canonical_name: ordinary differential equation maximal-solution and continuation family
literal_source_claim_en: the maximal interval of existence of a solution
candidate_family_not_credited_as_stateme: Under source-selected local existence and uniqueness hypotheses for an ordinary differential equation, construct the maximal solution through prescribed initial data on a maximal interval and prove exactly the source-selected maximality or endpoint-continuation conclusion.
statement_blocker: The catalog does not select maximal-solution existence, an endpoint extension equivalence, compact continuation, escape from compacta, norm blow-up, or global existence. It also omits the equation, open domain, state space, vector-field regularity, uniqueness premise, solution and extension predicates, interval order, endpoint direction, and boundary cases. Choosing any standard variant would add proposition-changing mathematics.
domain_and_universes: Open: an exact source must fix autonomous or time-dependent dynamics, scalar, finite-dimensional, or Banach state, the open spacetime domain, time and state scalar fields, norms and topology, and the representation of partial-domain curves.
conclusion: Open: the repository does not say whether to assert a unique maximal solution, characterize extendibility, force escape from compacta or norm blow-up, or deduce global existence.
degenerate_case_status: No case is excluded at intake because no proposition is selected; every listed endpoint and domain case must be resolved by the statement phase.
candidate_scope_not_credited: existence and uniqueness of a maximal solution through each initial point under unique local solvability
equivalence between extension beyond a finite endpoint and convergence of a graph subsequence to an interior point of the vector-field domain
extension when a solution graph remains or recurs in a suitable compact subset
escape from every compact subset at a finite endpoint of a maximal solution
norm blow-up at a finite endpoint in a whole finite-dimensional state space
global existence under boundedness, linear growth, or another a priori estimate
degenerate_cases_to_resolve: empty, singleton, disconnected, half-open, closed, unbounded, or all-real time domains
finite versus infinite left and right endpoints and one-sided versus two-sided maximality
initial time on a boundary rather than in the interior of the solution interval
zero-dimensional or trivial state spaces, zero vector fields, equilibrium and already-global solutions
nonunique local solutions under mere continuity and whether maximal solutions are chosen or unique
solutions that approach the boundary of a proper open spacetime domain while their norm stays bounded
compact escape versus norm divergence in nonproper, infinite-dimensional, or non-whole state spaces
extension by equality on the old domain versus germ, restriction, or almost-everywhere equivalence
excluded_substitutions: THM-M-1332 Picard-Lindelof local existence and uniqueness alone
THM-M-1333 Peano existence under continuity alone
THM-M-1336 comparison theorems or THM-M-1337 Gronwall inequality
a local solution on one fixed compact interval presented as a maximal solution
a structure that assumes maximality, extendibility, compact escape, blow-up, or global existence as a field
Zorn maximality without the source-selected uniqueness and endpoint conclusion when those are part of the target
norm blow-up or global existence inferred without the required whole-space, finite-dimensional, compactness, growth, or a priori-bound hypotheses
the untrusted catalog label verified as human-source or Lean kernel evidence
